Located at the prominent address of 300 Frankfort Road, Monaca, Pennsylvania 15061-2295, Horsehead Corporation stands as a highly significant entity in the annals of American industrial manufacturing and chemical processing. For decades, this sprawling site along the banks of the Ohio River served as the beating heart of Horsehead’s expansive metallurgical and chemical operations. As a leading manufacturer of specialty zinc and zinc-based products, the company played a crucial role in supplying fundamental raw materials to a vast array of global industries, including the automotive, construction, and agricultural sectors.

At its Monaca facility, Horsehead Corporation operated one of the largest zinc smelters in the United States. The company was particularly renowned for its innovative environmental technologies, most notably its pioneering work in recycling electric arc furnace (EAF) dust—a hazardous byproduct of the steelmaking process. Through complex chemical and metallurgical processes, Horsehead safely transformed this industrial waste into valuable, high-purity zinc products, such as zinc oxide, zinc dust, and various metallic alloys. These materials were essential for galvanizing steel, manufacturing rubber tires, and producing numerous vital chemical compounds.

Beyond its operational achievements, the 300 Frankfort Road location represents a massive industrial footprint that anchored the local Beaver County economy for generations. While the sweeping tides of economic and industrial transition eventually led to the closure of the Monaca smelter—paving the way for the site's high-profile sale and redevelopment into a major modern petrochemical complex—the legacy of Horsehead Corporation remains deeply woven into the region's history. The company's long tenure in Monaca stands as a lasting testament to Pennsylvania's rich heritage of chemical generation, metallurgical innovation, and heavy industrial prowess.
